source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Continue crisis-capacity practices as the preferred routine standard even after PPE supplies recover.","B":"Use crisis-capacity practices to eliminate required PPE during direct patient care.","C":"Limit crisis-capacity practices to administrative staff rather than clinical personnel.","D":"Use crisis-capacity practices temporarily when conventional and contingency measures cannot meet demand."}}
source_row.rationale: CDC/NIOSH distinguishes conventional, contingency, and crisis capacity. Crisis strategies are temporary measures for severe shortages and are not a substitute for routine practice once supply improves. Option D is correct; A, B, and C misstate their purpose and scope.
source_row.source_detail: Crisis-capacity strategies section: crisis measures are used temporarily during known shortages when conventional and contingency capacity cannot meet demand; they carry higher risk and should be discontinued as supply conditions improve. CDC/NIOSH page updated 2024-10-22; currentness live-rechecked 2026-08-15.
